summary: Preserved candidate PR 664's attention-TP padding and eager fail-closed boundary, independently reproduced review PR 3252's exact stale DSA token-metadata acceptance at candidate commit 183f57d6899bbb1df7a273383fa779ad94bffae7, and extended the DSA physical-extent contract to every directly token-indexed metadata buffer used by the indexer/top-k paths.

tests.what_was_measured: The exact candidate accepted physical_tokens=4 with dsa_seqlens_expanded, token_to_batch_idx, and both indexer range arrays retaining only 3 rows.
The corrected validator rejected the same metadata before model attention/KV side effects and reported all observed extents.
14 focused tests passed, covering actual ForwardBatch plan tracking, eager runner rejection, corrected DSA tokenwise extent validation, and GPU DSA padding.
On AMD Instinct MI350X, GPU metadata [11, 12, 13, 0] matched an independent attention-TP ceiling-alignment reference for four physical rows.

gpu_execution.evidence: The DSA padding kernel-facing tensor calculation executed on AMD Instinct MI350X with ROCm 7.2.26015 and matched the independent reference.

remaining_limitations: No DeepSeek DSA model weights or qualified end-to-end speculative DSA fixture were available, so full model-level attention/indexer/schedule/KV execution remains unverified. The provided tiny Llama fixture cannot qualify the different DSA architecture and was not treated as evidence. No C++/FlyDSL source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable. CUDA-only and distributed paths were not exercised.
